coverage.note: Federal corporation and grant records resolve the active legal entity and not-for-profit boundary; ownership remains null because no equity owner applies.
The federal registered office, public mailing route and current Canadian partner facilities establish a durable Canadian footprint.
Official service and government program sources define testbed, living-lab, commercialization and SME-support roles.
Published test types and network environments are concrete, while capacity, configuration limits, security accreditation and SLA remain unpublished.
Current services and a 2026 partner lab launch establish activity, but independently accepted participant performance is not public.
ENGINE and named partner facilities are current; no public customer acceptance or participant outcome is generalized beyond those records.

attempts: Official pages repeated secure and isolated infrastructure claims, while unrelated defence labs and a job description surfaced. No durable CENGN defence contract, classified-handling authority, Controlled Goods status, ISO 27001, SOC 2, Protected B or other recognized accreditation was found.
coverage.note: The final lane found no CENGN defence procurement, classified authority or recognized security certification.
Federal funding and named Ericsson, CNIMI, Waterloo and Rogers roles are explicit and separated from ownership.
A service email, contact page, telephone and expression-of-interest path provide a clear route into action.
Ericsson's dated account identifies the April 16, 2026 Advanced Manufacturing Living Lab launch.
Nine sources span federal registry/program, first-party technical, commercial partner and university partner owners.
Registered office and mailing address are different functions, not conflicting identities; government funding and program partnership do not imply ownership.

saturation.stopReason: Security/accreditation/procurement probing added no CENGN defence contract, classified authorization or recognized certification. Independent participant/capacity probing added two current partner relationships but no price, queue, SLA, acceptance rate or accepted performance. Those final lanes bounded rather than changed the identity, mandate, access path or reviewer action, so marginal yield is low.

warnings: CENGN is a federally incorporated soliciting not-for-profit and program/testbed operator, not an equity-owned vendor. The $45 million is a non-repayable federal contribution for ENGINE, not ownership or a guaranteed downstream award. Public sources do not establish defence procurement, classified handling authority, recognized security certification, service capacity, pricing, queue, SLA or independently accepted participant performance.
